speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual start—could you describe how you're feeling and what symptoms you've been experiencing? I need to know more about your current condition.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the self-resolving knee pain, could you describe the specific appearance and location of the skin lesions on your wrist? Also, have you noticed any joint swelling or redness in the affected wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Sporotrichosis (rose gardener's disease). The combination of a camping trip in Minnesota, a history of migratory joint pain (likely an initial inoculation site), and now painful, violaceous nodules/vesicles progressing to the wrist with regional lymphangitis is highly characteristic. I am requesting images of the wrist lesions to confirm the distribution. REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist_Lesion_Close_Up. Please confirm if you recall handling wild berries, roses, or soil directly during your trip.
